normalized.governing_thought: fix promotions, shrink, delivery pricing and loss-making stores rather than cutting store hours, and start with the tested, low-capital moves now
executive_summary: Wages are not the main cause of the decline. Operating margin fell 2.35 pts (3.37% → 1.02%, FY2023–25). Gross margin explains 1.02 pts (promotions −0.70, shrink −0.50, partly offset by private label +0.18) and e-commerce fulfillment 0.84 pts. Store labor explains only 0.30 pts, because fewer hours per $ of sales (−6%) absorbed most of the +9.4% wage rise.

Management’s draft (cut hours 8%, freeze e-commerce) would not reach the target. The $14.5M saving would probably shrink to ~$4.5M, because thinly staffed stores run 3.1% shrink against 2.3% in the best-staffed. That leaves FY2026 operating income near the $20M covenant and the FY2028 margin at about 1–1.5%. The freeze also locks in an e-commerce loss of $10.4M a year.

Instead, pull four groups of levers worth ~$29M a year by FY2028. Commercial (cut loss-making promotions, rebuild vendor funding, grow private label) $13.5M · store operations (cut shrink, reshape rather than cut labor) $6.4M · re-price home delivery, which is kept $2.5M · exit the nine stores with negative four-wall EBITDA $6.6M.

This protects the covenant but reaches 3.0% only if upside lands. Base case: FY2026 operating income $24.8M (covenant $20M) and FY2028 margin 2.65%, after absorbing a $6.8M wage step. Reaching 3.0% needs $4.9M more, about one-third of the $15M upside we identified. Capital needed: ~$20M of the $25M envelope.

What to do first (next 90 days). Roll out the tested delivery fee chain-wide. Drop the money-losing promotions and make vendor co-funding a condition of every event. Cancel the blanket hours cut and move hours to produce and receiving. Serve notice on the six expiring leases. Rebid the delivery contract instead of accepting +3%.

slides.title: We started from a hypothesis and tested it. Three of six conditions held fully and two partly, and the evidence changed the answer in three ways

claims.claim: Initial hypothesis: the decline is driven by promotions, shrink and loss-making delivery, not wages. Fixing those, rather than cutting store hours, gets Harlow back to 3.0% by FY2028.
1. Wages are a minor driver of the decline — Supported
evidence: Labor = 0.30 of 2.35 pts (13%). Wage +9.4%, hours per $1,000 of sales −6.0%

claims.claim: 2. Gross-margin erosion comes from Harlow’s own choices — Supported
evidence: Promo mix −0.70 + shrink −0.50 + private label +0.18 = −1.02 pts, which matches the actual change exactly

claims.claim: 3. Promotions can be cut back without losing core shoppers — Partly: keep value investment in ValuMart trade areas
evidence: 38% of events lose money; price perception worsened anyway (33% → 41% "more expensive"). But stores near ValuMart run −4.2% comps

claims.claim: 4. Delivery is the e-commerce problem and can be fixed while keeping it — Partly: re-pricing closes only ~¼ of the loss
evidence: Delivered order −$12.34, click-and-collect −$1.64. The fee test recovers ~$2.5M, but delivery still loses ~$9 an order

claims.claim: 5. Cutting labor further would backfire — Supported
evidence: Shrink 3.1% in the least-staffed quartile vs 2.3% in the most-staffed; managers report skipped checks (correlation, not proven cause)

claims.claim: 6. The fixes reach 3.0% within $25M and keep the covenant — Not on the base case
evidence: Covenant holds in the base case ($24.8M). FY2028 margin 2.65%, so 3.0% needs upside

claims.claim: How the answer changed: (a) all nine loss-making stores are now in the core plan; (b) labor moved from "do not touch" to "reshape": −2% net hours, taken from the most heavily staffed stores; (c) 3.0% is presented honestly as base case 2.65% plus a named stretch plan

slides.title: Gross margin (1.02 pts) and e-commerce fulfillment (0.84 pts) explain nearly 80% of the 2.35-pt margin decline. Store labor explains 0.30 pts

claims.claim: Operating margin bridge FY2023 → FY2025
evidence: Chart: FY2023 margin 3.37; Promotional mix −0.70; Shrink −0.50; Private-label mix +0.18; E-commerce fulfillment −0.84; Store labor −0.30; Occupancy & energy −0.20; Other SG&A −0.0001; FY2025 margin 1.02
Gross margin: −1.02 pts

claims.claim: Promotions are the largest single driver
evidence: Promo share rose 24% → 29% of sales at a 14-pt lower margin: −0.70 pts (≈ $10.5M)

claims.claim: E-commerce fulfillment grew from $5.2M to $18.1M as orders tripled: −0.84 pts (≈ $12.6M)
Store labor added only 0.30 pts (≈ $4.5M), and occupancy 0.20 pts; Other SG&A held at 4.7% of sales
Wages are a real cost pressure but not the main cause: 87% of the decline lies elsewhere

slides.title: Deeper promotions have not defended traffic. 38% of events lose money and more shoppers now see Harlow as expensive

evidence: Promotional sales, % of sales: FY2023 24; FY2024 26.2; FY2025 29
Shoppers who say Harlow is "more expensive": FY2023 33; FY2025 41
Stores within 3 miles of a ValuMart still ran −4.2% comps (vs +1.1%), and the "expensive" score rose 8 pts
Price-perception survey n = 3,100

evidence: 38% of FY2025 events lost money even after counting their extra units
Harlow also now funds 54% of markdowns itself, up from 45%

evidence: top reasons to shop Harlow are fresh produce (58%) and convenience (44%), not price

Vendor funding: 14% × $435.9M = $61.0M = 54% of gross markdowns; gross ≈ $113M; 1 pt ≈ $1.13M
E-commerce: Sales 1,331k × $96 = $127.8M; incremental contribution $7.7M; net fulfillment $18.1M; Net = −$10.4M

FY2028 base: ratio levers × 0.941; margin = $37.5M ÷ $1,411.9M = 2.65%

normalized.recommendation: Approve the margin plan in place of the draft labor cut: four lever groups (commercial, store operations, re-price home delivery which is kept, exit the nine stores with negative four-wall EBITDA) worth ~$29M a year by FY2028, target 3.0% operating margin with a base case of 2.65% and a named stretch plan; withdraw the blanket 8% hours cut. Release ~$20.1M of the $25M one-time envelope in stages, lever by lever against business cases, with $4.9M held in reserve. Approve in principle a vote on the three stores with leases beyond 2027 (two-quarter fix-or-exit plan; formal vote in Q2 FY2027). Endorse the e-commerce approach: keep delivery but re-price it and favor click-and-collect; if delivery still loses more than $6M by end-FY2027, the board reviews a slimmer delivery offer.
